issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires that the Person entity defines a constructor that initializes firstName and lastName (problem_statement.md line 24). However, both the template and solution Person classes only provide a no-argument constructor (public Person() {}) and do not provide a constructor that initializes firstName and lastName. This contradicting requirement in the problem statement may confuse students (they may expect to find or implement such a constructor) and is an unintentional structural inconsistency between the specification and the provided code.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an explicit constructor that initializes firstName and lastName to the Person class while keeping the no-argument constructor required by JPA. For example: public Person(String firstName, String lastName) { this.firstName = firstName; this.lastName = lastName; }. Also update the problem statement if the constructor requirement was not intended, to avoid misleading students.
